newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Saudi petchem delays support LPG exports - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Saudi petchem delays support LPG exports - MEES.

text.p: Saudi Aramco's liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) exports are likely to run above Saudi estimates because of delays in new local petrochemical plants, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

"The uncertainty surrounding the start-up of...liquids-driven petrochemical projects is likely to mean that when the century ends the producer will be exporting at least two million tons more than the 10 million tons a year forecast for 1999," the Cyprus-based MEES newsletter reported.
Saudi Aramco had projected a sharp drop in LPG exports by the end of the decade because of growing demand for propane and butane at new petrochemical plants planned in the kingdom.
"Evidence is mounting that both the extent and timing of this export reduction may be overstated," MEES said.
Saudi LPG exports had averaged 14.5 million tonnes in 1996, against a forecast of 13.8 million tonnes and were actually higher than the 1995 level of just over 14 million tonnes.
"Rising internal demand had been expected to result in a fall of exports...This reduction did not materialise."

Though demand for LPG in Saudi Arabia's expanding petrochemical sector was increasing, the timetable for petrochemical plants originally expected to come onstream in 1998-1999 was now slipping back to the turn of the decade.

"Construction delays and other slippages in project implementation schedules mean that many of these plants will not be ready for commissioning until after the turn of the century, much later than originally planned," MEES reported.
Only one project -- an aromatics plant being built at Yanbu by Saudi Basic Industries Corp affiliate Ibn Rushd -- was under construction and likely to be completed by 2000.
Even a new, LPG-based MTBE plant by SABIC affiliate SADAF which was inaugurated last month was operating at reduced operating rates because of weak MTBE export markets.
Firms planning new ethylene crackers had looked at configurations that use a lower proportion of propane while a major aromatic project would use naphtha-based technology.

"Whether Aramco will be able to maintain (LPG) exports above the 14 million tonne mark for 1997 and thereafter until Ibn Rushd comes on-stream in late 1998 remains to be seen but the betting is that it will," MEES reported.
Aramco is the world's largest LPG exporter with its major customers in Japan.
